The Chagai hill area in Balochistan remained subject to volcanic activity in the past. The
volcanoes of the area are extinct but their eroded craters still exist. The Koh i Sultan is the most
spectacular of these craters and its elevation is about 2334 meters above sea level.
Mud volcanoes are also located in some areas of Balochistan. These volcanoes are created by
eruption of mud, water and gases. They are not igneous in nature. Chandragup mud volcanoes
exist in Hingot National Park of Lasbella district in Balochistan. The three main mud volcanoes
are called Chandragup 1, Chandragup 2 and Chandragup 3. Jebel e Ghurab is another mud
volcanolocatedinBalochistan.
